name: No-Boil Chicken Pasta Casserole with Artichokes and Peas

prose.intro_html:
Some nights you do not have a second pot in you, let alone a colander to wash. This is the casserole for those nights. It is a no-boil, dump-and-bake number, which means the penne goes into the dish dry and cooks right in the sauce while the oven does the thinking. You stir chicken, artichoke hearts, and peas into a blender-smooth sauce built on cottage cheese and Boursin, cover it with foil, and walk away.

Here is why I keep coming back to it. One serving lands at {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein, and that protein is doing honest work: lean chicken breast, cottage cheese, and parmesan all pulling together. That is a real dinner, not a snack that pretends to be one. And because there is no boiling, no browning, and no babysitting, the active time is about as short as cooking gets.
prose.shop_smart:
Buy the penne dry and buy it in the box, not fresh. Dry pasta is what makes the no-boil trick work, because it drinks up the thin sauce as it bakes. Grab enough to cover the full batch in one go so you are not opening a second brand halfway through.

The chicken breast is the star, so this is where your money goes and where it should. Buy it boneless and skinless and cube it into one-inch pieces yourself; a family pack costs less to fill the batch than pre-cut strips. If breasts are on a good week at your store, this is the recipe to build around them.

Boursin comes in the little 5.2 ounce foil-wrapped rounds, garlic and fine herbs. You will use a couple of rounds plus a bit, so plan on picking up the packages you need rather than expecting one to stretch. Cottage cheese and parmesan you buy in the tubs and wedges you already know; grate the parmesan fresh if you can, it melts down golden in a way the sandy pre-grated stuff does not. Canned artichoke hearts and a bag of frozen peas round it out, both pantry-and-freezer staples that keep, so nothing here forces you to cook it tonight.
prose.make_it:
Heat the oven to 400 degrees F. Lightly grease your baking dish and set it aside. A quick word on the dish: this is a 14-serving batch, so it is bigger than one standard 9x13. Split it across two 9x13 dishes or use one large deep roasting pan so the pasta can lie flat and stay submerged.

Make the sauce in a blender or food processor. Add the cottage cheese, the crumbled Boursin, the minced garlic, the fresh lemon juice, the lemon zest, and the sea salt. Blend until it is smooth, then pour in the chicken broth and blend again until it is completely incorporated. It will look very thin, and that is exactly right; that thinness is the water your dry pasta is going to drink.

Now dump and assemble. Lay the dry penne across the bottom, then scatter the cubed chicken, the peas, and the chopped artichoke hearts over the top. Pour the blended sauce over everything and make sure every piece of pasta is submerged. Anything poking out will dry into a hard bit, so tuck it under.

Cover tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes. Pull it out, take off the foil, and give it a good stir. The pasta should be a touch undercooked here, which is what you want. Scatter the parmesan over the top and return it to the oven, uncovered, for another 5 to 10 minutes to set and turn golden; you can nudge the temperature up to chase that color. If the pasta already feels done when you stir, just add the parmesan and skip the extra bake.

Let it rest at least 10 minutes before you serve or portion. The sauce keeps tightening as it cools, so that rest is what turns a loose bake into a sliceable casserole. Finish with the chopped parsley or basil.
prose.portion_html:
This batch is built for 14 containers, and the fair way to split a casserole is to weigh it, not eyeball it. Once it has rested, set your empty dish or pan on the scale and zero it, or weigh a clean container first and subtract. Take the total cooked weight, divide by 14, and that is your target grams per container. Scoop to the number rather than counting spoonfuls, and every lid closes on the same {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein.

Work edge to center so the artichoke, peas, and chicken land evenly and nobody opens the sad all-pasta container on Thursday. Cool them uncovered for a few minutes before you seal, then refrigerate.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Here is the part that matters when the receipt prints. This whole thing comes to ${{cost_ps}} per serving, and for that you are getting {{protein}} grams of protein and a genuine dinner, not a side dish with delusions. Chicken breast, cottage cheese, and parmesan are not cheap by accident; they are cheap per serving because this batch stretches them across 14 lids.

Cook once, eat all week, and let the math work for you instead of against you.

head.description: A no-boil, dump-and-bake chicken pasta casserole with artichokes, peas, and a creamy cottage cheese and Boursin sauce. Scales to 14 high-protein meal-prep servings at 603 calories and 54.8 grams of protein each.
head.keywords: no boil chicken pasta casserole, dump and bake casserole, high protein meal prep, chicken artichoke pasta, cottage cheese pasta bake, budget meal prep dinner, penne casserole, meal prep chicken
steps: Heat the oven to 400 degrees F and lightly grease your baking dish. This 14-serving batch needs more room than a single 9x13, so use two 9x13 dishes or one large deep roasting pan.

In a blender or food processor, combine the cottage cheese, crumbled Boursin, minced garlic, fresh lemon juice, lemon zest, and sea salt. Blend until smooth, then add the chicken broth and blend again until fully incorporated. The sauce will be very thin, which is correct.

Lay the dry penne across the bottom of the dish, then scatter the cubed chicken, peas, and chopped artichoke hearts over the top. Pour the blended sauce over everything and make sure all the pasta is submerged.

Cover tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes. Remove the foil, stir well, then top with the parmesan and return to the oven uncovered for 5 to 10 minutes until golden and set. Nudge the temperature up if you want more color.
Let the casserole rest at least 10 minutes so the sauce sets, then finish with chopped parsley or basil and serve or portion.
